LTX-2.3 on Mac: files, RAM and published times

LTX-2.3 is a 22B DiT-based audio-video foundation model from Lightricks that generates synchronized video and audio in a single model. On a Mac it runs through community MLX ports, and no official Lightricks Mac benchmark was found.

Lightricks · Updated 2026-11-04
Short answer

LTX-2.3 runs on an NVIDIA GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. Published run (source): RTX 4060, 8 GB, ComfyUI GGUF workflow, 720p 5 s in about 190 s, 32 GB RAM.

Answer

LTX-2.3 runs on a Mac with 24 GB or more. A published run on Apple M5 Pro · 24 GB used ltx-2-mlx-swift int8 streamed, 704x512, 121 frames, 150 s (source).

Does it fit your NVIDIA GPU's VRAM?

Runs · Stated means the linked model card, app maker or NVIDIA says a GPU with that much VRAM runs the model; Runs · Published names the card of a dated run. Fits with offload means the main model weights fit in VRAM with a 15% margin but the full set does not: the text encoder and VAE run from system RAM, which is slower. Exceeds VRAM means even the main weights are too large for the card. Mac runs never count here.

Which Mac software routes are listed?

  • ComfyUI

    Official

    Formats: safetensors, gguf. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    On Apple Silicon ComfyUI runs on PyTorch MPS, not MLX. GGUF files need the separate city96/ComfyUI-GGUF custom node. Resident size is the sum of the weights, an upper bound: ComfyUI can unload models between stages and publishes no per-model Mac peak.

    Sources: ComfyUI README · ComfyUI system requirements · ComfyUI CLI arguments · ComfyUI-GGUF README

  • dgrauet/ltx-2-mlx

    Community

    Formats: mlx. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    Pure MLX port of LTX-2 for Apple Silicon with its own MLX weight packs. --low-ram streams transformer blocks from disk. Resident size is the sum of the weights, an upper bound.

    Sources: dgrauet ltx-2-mlx README

  • Lightricks/LTX-2 ltx-pipelines

    Official

    Formats: safetensors. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    No Lightricks Mac benchmark was found.

    Sources: LTX-2 README

  • appautomaton/ltx-video-mlx

    Community

    Formats: safetensors. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    Sources: appautomaton ltx-video-mlx README

What does the official configuration say?

"Official tested stack: Python >=3.12, CUDA version >12.7, PyTorch ~= 2.7. No official Mac memory figure was found."

Source: LTX-2.3 model card · Read 2026-10-24.

What known issues should you check?

  • Known issue 1

    The card lists only a CUDA test stack, and no official Mac memory statement or Lightricks Mac benchmark was found.

    Source: LTX-2.3 model card · Read 2026-10-24

  • Known issue 2

    The appautomaton benchmark carries no run date. The date shown is the date of the pinned commit.

    Source: appautomaton ltx-video-mlx performance notes · Read 2026-10-24

  • Known issue 3

    Width and height must be divisible by 32, and the frame count must be divisible by 8 plus 1.

    Source: LTX-2.3 model card · Read 2026-10-24

Frequently asked questions

How fast is LTX-2.3 on a Mac?

appautomaton's MLX port generated 121 frames at 512x512 in about 101 s end to end on an M5 Max with 128 GB, using 4-bit weights and 8 steps, with roughly 53 GB peak RAM. The source gives no run date, so the date shown is the commit date.

What does the LTX-2.3 download include?

Each main checkpoint is one file bundling the transformer, the video and audio VAEs and the text projection. The Gemma 3 text encoder is downloaded separately, and width and height must be divisible by 32.
